newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end slightly up, eyes on Sulzer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end slightly up, eyes on Sulzer.

text.p: 1540 GMT - Swiss shares recovered from a dip below 4,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) around midday to end slightly higher as investors concentrated on Sulzer.
Shares in Sulzer soared around 17 percent on plans to sell-off some 25 percent of its Sulzer Medica unit.
Dealers said U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's speech before the Senate Budget Committe was well received by markets.
Trading volumes were described as relatively high. Future development depended largely on Wall Street's moves, a trader noted.
* The SMI was up 13.7 points, or 0.34 percent, to 4,023.2.
* Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended at 2,581.43 points, up 6.76 points, or 0.26 percent, from Monday's close.

* Sulzer shares jumped 144 francs to 982 after reaching an all-time high of 1,000 francs in early trade. The move to float 25 percent of its Sulzer Medica was seen favourable for the group, dealers said.
* Nestle added six francs to 1,475, although the 7.1 percent rise in 1996 group sales to 60.5 billion francs was within expectations, a trader noted.
Nestle also expected profit growth in 1996 to exceed growth seen in sales.

* UBS outperformed the other major banks on a recommendation by Lehman Brothers, a dealer said. UBS bearer shares added 18 francs, or 1.58 percent, to 1,155 francs. CS Holding eased 0.75 francs to 137.75. SBC gave up 0.25 francs to 247.50.
* Among insurers, Winterthur profited from its 2.5 percent stake in Sulzer, dealers said. Winterthur rose 15 francs, nearly two percent, to 793.
* Roche certificates traded evenly at 11,170 francs.
* Swissair climbed 38 francs, or 3.28 percent, to 1,195 francs.
* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), implicit volatilities were lower. The volatilities index, calculated by Bank Leu, was 0.15 percentage points lower at 17.48 percent.
Total volume in options reached 131,595 contracts, of which 24,120 were SMI options.
The total call to put ratio stood at one to 1.12. Swiss Re stood out with a high share of puts, a dealer said. 8,257 Swiss Re calls and 14,454 puts changed hands.
On the futures side, 5,023 SMI futures were traded.
